children: : The Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) auctioned treasury bills (T-bills) at a total value of EGP 110 billion over two issues on Thursday, September 17, according to the CBE’s data.
The first tranche, amounting to EGP 30 billion, holds an 182-day tenor until March 23, 2027.
Valued at EGP 80 billion, the second auction will mature in 364 days on September 21, next year.
T-bills are short-term government securities offered by the CBE on behalf of the Ministry of Finance. They are mainly used to help the government finance its short-term funding needs.
